subject: Re: iMerit BiWeekly Sync Notes
text:
Hi Abinash,

Thanks for reaching out, here is my best understanding of the answers to
your questions.

   - *Overwrite Logic:* Team checked their review tasks and found only 1
   classification done by any one surgeon can only be approved. If the same
   'Task label' by another surgeon is being approved, then it automatically
   asks to 'Overwrite' the earlier approved label. What is the recommended
   minimum threshold for approving labels to avoid this overwrite scenario?
   - If both annotators created an acceptable annotation, go ahead and
      accept both and overwrite the second label.  The reviewer should also be
      able to edit the annotation before final submission.  From a
      workflow perspective, the main thing that matters is that the final label
      looks good.  The reject tool is used if the label is incorrect
or it would
      be desirable for the original labeler to review the label so they can
      improve their annotations.
   - *Multiple Start/End Points:* Team is finding it difficult to manage
   tasks with numerous start and end points within a single video (e.g., 10-20
   different timelines for the same task within a 30-minute video). The tool
   doesn't allow us to disagree on only one or two specific timelines without
   rejecting the entire task. Similarly, when disagreements between surgeons
   exist on only a few time points, approving the task becomes challenging.
   How can we effectively handle these scenarios?
   - This may be a limitation of the tool and we may need to change the
      workflow to make it easier to review.  In the future, we should probably
      make different segments different entries in the timeline so they can be
      labeled individually.  For now, the reviewer can accept the
closest one and
      the edit the label to be correct before final submission.
   - *Encord Team Assistance:* We would greatly appreciate the Encord
   team's availability this week to help us resolve these review workflow
   q

subject: Re: Encord <> Mujin | Trial Next Steps
text:
Hi Charlotte and Steffan,
Sorry for the delayed response.
Thank you for creating an overview of criteria. I have copied the table below and updated it with some of my inputs.
Two aspects I have explained in more detail, and have summarized that in the table.
As for QA workflows. Not sure how we can determine with a trial that overall a reduced QA time is achievable. That would require running multiple projects from setup to production (takes 1~3 months each). From what I gather the trial would be about a week or so. What I had in mind was to use an internal development project to simulate the first stage of that process, and determine how easy it would be to reach the first state of QA = 0.1% error rate (once an hour), which is 100x of our production level error rate.
Scalable as for team size is not a requirement for us. Kind of the opposite. What we aim for is scalable in deployment size. To achieve that we look for tooling to automate the process as much as possible and have almost no human intervention in the loop. What I imagine, is to hook-up a robotic system, where the integration tool between robotic system and encord will collect and upload the data. Then encord will be able to process the data and provide a qualitative report. E.g. 99% of the data was giving right the results (e.g. our QA level is not achieved yet). This 1% error is caused by reasons A, B, C. Fine-tune the network with a certain part of that data, then achieve 0.1% error rate by doing that.
The ease of obtaining the data to fine-tune and the quality of that data (such that the required error rate is achieved) is a determining factor.
Next steps:

  *
I'll share a date in May when we can collect data. Some of the hardware delivered from US is delayed, so I hope that the hardware setup can start soon.
  *
I'll first need to make a proposal to my division head (which is not Hajime). To do so, I'll have to do similar comparisons with other tool providers, before I can continue to have that con
